A woman based on the supplied portrait is the keeper at the bench; use the supplied portrait for her face and hair, retaining its soft oval face, wide dark eyes, soft rosy lips, short black bob and fine separated bangs. The room is being packed for departure: tied archive boxes occupy the shelves, empty circular dust marks show where recording reels stood, and her closed travel bag waits against her hip. Her charcoal wool dress has a simple square neckline, a softly fitted waist and small creases from bending over the bench; warm light grazes her collarbones and her unguarded, concentrated face. She has just pushed the apparatus's long black ebonite lever downward with her right hand, her fingers wrapped around its full insulated grip and her bent elbow beside her ribs. Her left hand lightly holds the travel bag strap at her hip. Both feet support her behind the waist-high bench, with her torso leaning only slightly toward the reachable lever. The invention is a brass and glazed-ceramic discharge annunciator assembled as a real piece of equipment. There is visible electrical discharge at metal electrodes: on the raised brass deck a single thin, jagged white-violet spark bridges the clearly separated tips of two rounded copper terminals. Each copper terminal sits on a separate glazed-ceramic standoff; their opposed rounded ends define the compact air gap above the brass deck. The crooked luminous thread runs all the way from the left copper tip to the right copper tip, meeting metal at both ends while a dark pocket of air remains around the flash. Farther to the right, on a separate pointed charging comb, tiny diffuse violet corona brushes cling close to the sharp metal points. The bright gap flash and the faint local corona remain distinct in scale and texture. Red and black braided cables visibly terminate at the apparatus base and its cylindrical coil enclosure; a paired insulated lead continues from that enclosure to a small beacon lamp beneath thick glass at the left end of the bench. The amber lamp has just come alive, its reflected oval appearing on the worn wood while she looks toward it with parted lips and a restrained exhale. The lever, cable route, illuminated lamp and packed room connect the final activation to her impending departure. Photograph from slightly to the left of the apparatus at chest height in a vertical knee-up environmental portrait: her face, gripping hand, gap terminals, corona comb and lamp occupy one readable layer. A 50 mm lens at moderate depth of field keeps these connections legible; the archive shelves recede gently. Dusk enters the high salt-streaked window, the amber lamp warms her skin, and violet discharge casts small local reflections on glazed ceramic. Natural skin texture, scuffed brass, ceramic glaze and faint low-light grain give the invention physical weight.
